title: Anatomically Realistic Neonatal Heart Model for Use in Neonatal Patient Simulators
protocol: Obtain institutional approvals before patient imaging.
Acquire a thoracic MRI scan in DICOM format.
Import the DICOM file using processing software.
Select the area of the heart muscle on each MRI slice using 'Editing Masks'.
Create a new sketch layer and segment the two atria and two ventricles separately.
Do not segment valves between the atria and ventricles, and between the ventricles and arteries.
Render the muscle and chambers into separate 3D representations using 'Calculate 3D' menu item.
Export the heart muscle and four chambers as five STereoLithography (.stl) files using 'STL+' menu item with optimal resolution settings.
Load the .stl files into CAD software.
Repair the .stl files for overlapping triangles and bad edges using the fix wizard menu item.
Save the repaired .stl files.
Add the pulmonary and aortic valve files to their respective ventricle locations.
Sketch two arching cylinders of 5 mm diameter from the top of each valve using the 'sketch tab > circle' feature.
Extrude both circular cylinder surfaces until they reach the horizontal position using the 'features tab > sweep boss/base'.
Merge the valve parts with their respective ventricles and arteries.
Draw vertical cylinders of 5 mm diameter from the base of each chamber and arched cylinders using the 'sketch tab > circle' feature.
Extrude these cylinders to a length of 40 mm using the 'features tab > extrude boss/base'.
Ensure each cylinder protrudes into its respective chamber.
Sketch semicircles on top of the six cylinders for differential notches using the 'sketch tab > sketch circle' menu item.
Create different depth indentations by selecting the 'feature tab > cut/extrude' menu item.
Subtract the shapes of these cylinders from the chambers and arteries by right-clicking their solid bodies, then selecting 'combine', and choosing the 'subtract' setting.
Import the heart muscle model.
Start a new sketch and select all cylinder base sketches by holding down the 'shift' key.
Select the 'sketch tab > convert entities' menu item.
Select the 'sketch tab > offset entities' menu item to offset the sketches by 2 mm.
Extrude and merge these sketches by clicking the 'features tab > extrude boss/bass' menu item with the heart muscle model.
Repeat for the arching cylinders.
Merge these cylinders with the heart muscle model by clicking the 'features tab > extrude boss/bass' menu item.
Place a reference plane by clicking the 'features tab > reference geometry > plane'.
Click the 'sketch tab > square' menu item and sketch a square with a length and width that is 4 mm wider than the widest part of the heart muscle model.
Extrude this downwards with a thickness of 8 mm by clicking the 'features tab > extrude boss/base' menu item.
Merge this to the base of the six cylinders marking the 'merge parts' menu item.
On the four corners of the base, add 4 mm cubes using the same method.
Use a jetting printer for printing with rigid and rubber-like photopolymer materials installed.
Place the parts for printing on the print bed facing upwards (vertically).
Select the print settings to glossy.
For the four chambers as well as the pulmonary and aortic mold attachments, select the flexible S95 material.
For the other four mold parts, select the rigid print material.
Remove support material built up during printing by waterjet.
Place the cleaned mold parts in a 5% sodium hydroxide solution for 24 h.
Rinse the parts with cold water after removal from the solution.
Leave the parts to dry for 48 h before casting.
Spray all surfaces of all mold parts with a release agent, except the valves.
Wipe clean with tissue paper after spraying the release agent.
Leave treated mold parts to dry for 15 min.
Close the base of the mold and two side panels.
Place the mold on top of two spacers so the base is not in direct contact with the table surface.
Insert a silicone cartridge into the manual dispensing gun.
Add 5 mL of silicone from the dispensing gun to a measuring cup and mix using a toothpick.
Apply a generous amount of melted silicone to the negative and positive side of the right atria and ventricle valves using a toothpick.
Ensure there are no air bubbles in the applied silicone.
Connect the two chambers at the right valve angle, push them onto their respective cylinders of the base mold.
Repeat for the left side.
Attach the pulmonary and aortic arched cylinders similarly.
Leave these valves to solidify for 2 min.
Attach the top part of the mold.
Attach a static mixer to the cartridge, squeeze until silicone exits the nozzle, then release pressure.
Position the entire mold on two spacers, insert the gun into the 8-mm injection molding socket, and squeeze with low pressure over the course of 3 min.
Stop injecting the silicone when all air vents show signs of overflow.
Remove the mixer and place the mold onto the table surface to seal bottom air vents.
Leave the silicone to solidify for 30 min.
Pry open the top part of the mold using a metal spacer.
Remove one side part of the mold at a time using a metal spacer.
Detect any air bubbles on the heart exterior after releasing outer molds.
Pierce an air bubble with a scalpel and fill it with a small amount of silicone using a toothpick.
Leave the filled area to cure for another 30 minutes.
Use compressed air to blow the heart model off the base of the mold, holding it firmly with one hand.
Fill and pressurize the left ventricle with water using a syringe to release the inner mold.
Grab and pull out the left ventricle inner mold part using Magill forceps.
Fill and pressurize the right ventricle with water using a syringe to release the inner mold.
Grab and pull out the right ventricle inner mold part using Magill forceps.
Fill and pressurize the pulmonary artery with water using a syringe to release the inner mold.
Pull out the pulmonary artery inner mold part using Magill forceps carefully.
Fill and pressurize the aortic artery with water using a syringe to release the inner mold.
Grab and pull out the aortic artery inner mold part using Magill forceps.
Bind the two tubes leading directly downwards from the ventricles at the base of the heart model using tie wraps.
Remove access air vent strings by plucking them at the heart wall surface.
